subject: Oceanography
title: The Age of the Ocean Floor
description: A quick win: understand The Age of the Ocean Floor.

hook.text: No ocean floor on Earth is older than 200 million years—while continental rocks can be 4 billion years old.

buildup.text: Ocean crust is constantly created at ridges and destroyed at subduction zones—a perpetual recycling loop.

discovery.text: The youngest ocean floor is at the ridges (0 years old); the oldest is near subduction zones.

twist.text: This means the ocean floor we see today has no record of the first 96% of Earth's history.

climax.text: To study ancient oceans, geologists look at ophiolites—slabs of old ocean floor pushed onto land.

punchline.text: The ocean floor erases itself—and starts over every 200 million years.

quiz.question: Why is no ocean floor older than about 200 million years?
options: Subduction continuously destroys and recycles it
